setting: You all live in the Rhondda valleys in South Wales and sit on the committee of a village football club there. You have known each other for years through the club, from the touchline, the bar and the committee table. You all know each other's families, jobs and the club's history. Last time you were in touch, you were arguing about whether the pasties at the last quiz night had run out before the raffle.
opener: Asks the group to confirm by tonight who can attend Thursday's committee meeting.

Gareth.knows: You know Sian is the club treasurer, a steady, careful woman you have worked with for over a decade. You know Rhys is the youngest on the committee, a former player who now coaches the juniors and is always keen to change things.
Gareth.like: You are patient, dry and a bit old-fashioned, with a good line in deadpan jokes. You have firm opinions about proper minutes, paying bills on time and the sorry state of the changing-room roof.
Gareth.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when there is paperwork to chase or a decision to make.
Gareth.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you rarely use emoji or abbreviations.

Sian.knows: You know Gareth is the club secretary, an organised man who likes things written down. You know Rhys is the junior coach, a bit impulsive but well liked by the kids and their parents.
Sian.like: You are practical, warm and quick to laugh, and you have strong views on fair spending and never leaving a bill unpaid. You are not one for long debates, but you will say what you think.
Sian.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually to confirm money, numbers or a deadline.
Sian.style: You type with normal capitals and punctuation, use the odd emoji, and sometimes write "thx" or "ok".

Rhys.knows: You know Gareth is the secretary, a strict but fair older man who runs the club by the rulebook. You know Sian is the treasurer, sensible and organised, and the one who keeps everyone's budgets honest.
Rhys.like: You are energetic, cheeky and a bit impatient, with a quick sense of humour. You have opinions about training methods, kit and getting new players in.
Rhys.texts: You message the group quite often, especially with ideas and quick updates from the juniors.
Rhys.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation, use abbreviations like "tbh" and "rn", and sometimes add a laughing emoji.

private_lines.Gareth: You live in Treorchy with your wife Lynne, and you work as a caretaker at the local comprehensive school. You get up early, do your shift, come home for tea, and spend most evenings doing club paperwork at the kitchen table. Weekends are for the pitch and the bar.
private_lines.Sian: You live in Tonypandy with your dog, and you work as a pharmacy technician at the chemist on the main road. You work set shifts, walk the dog before and after work, and usually spend evenings catching up on admin or watching television. Your days run on routine.
private_lines.Rhys: You live in a flat in Ferndale with a flatmate, and you work as a PE teacher at a primary school in the valley. Your days are busy with school and training sessions, and you often get home late and crash on the sofa. You are out most weekends at fixtures.

situation: Three members of a village football club committee.

text: Committee meeting is Thursday at 7.30 in the clubhouse. Can everyone confirm by tonight whether they can come. We need the quorum and I would rather know now than on Thursday.
I can make it 👍
cant tbh. juniors train thurs 6 so ill be late if i make it at all. ill try
If you cannot attend in person, send any items to me in writing by Wednesday evening so they can be minuted.
ok will do. can we get new under 10s kit on the agenda pls. old ones are falling apart
Written request by Wednesday and it goes under AOB. Not before.
ok
thx gareth. can you bring the bar cash book too. need to sign off the float before the 1st
I will bring the cash book. It balances, if that is what you are asking.
😂 not asking. just checking. was short £4 last month remember
It was found in the tea urn.
lmao
just locked up after juniors. gents roof is dripping again. bucket's full already
Which bucket. I put a new one in October.
the new one. its not the bucket's fault
I will put it on the agenda under Premises. Do not empty it down the drain by the pitch. The neighbours complained about that last time.
can someone tell me if the roofer ever sent the quote
He sent it in August. It is in the folder marked Premises, which is in the drawer, which is also where the quote is.
😂 so no
Rhys, you have not confirmed Thursday. I would be grateful if you did.
ok im in. ill be there by 7.45. dont start
Half seven, please.
ha ok. dog's had his walk, im off to bed soon
Thursday then. Half seven.

ok. bit creepy tbh

Received. It is under AOB for Thursday.

Pasties are not on the agenda.

pasty = gareth agenda item confirmed 😂
The electrician came. It was the fuse, not the wiring. He charged £60. I will need a receipt for the accounts.
send me the receipt not the bill. bills dont go in the float book
There is only one kind of receipt, Sian.
😂 ok ok
still dont know about the van. asked a couple of the dads at training and nobody knows nothing
I asked at the comprehensive. Nothing reported. I have locked the gate on the car park side in any case.
gate was locked when i got there. so either someone else locked it or im losing it

😂 cheers gareth
off to bed soon. dog's had his walk and i've done the float sheet for thurs. gareth you can have it on the 1st

anyone else think that van was there for us
No. Vans are not for us. The only vehicle that comes to the clubhouse is the brewery lorry, and that is on Fridays.
just read this. rhys its 7am, go to bed 😂 i'm sure it's nothing. might be somebody collecting for a delivery
im up. van prob not for us. but i dont like the gate thing either. who locks a gate and then doesnt lock it

I locked the gate on Monday night and on Tuesday night. I have a key. The caretaker at the comprehensive has a key. Neither of us has reported anything. I would like the committee to look at a camera for the car park. I will put it under AOB with the kit and the roof.
a camera is £200 minimum and thats before the fitting. not coming out of the float. get 3 quotes and put them in writing gareth 😬
Three quotes. Agreed.
camera pls. we could ask the dads for a whip round. they all moan about their cars getting broke into anyway

It is in the folder. Page 3, behind the insurance schedule. You looked in the drawer and not the folder.

You are not a liar. You are an optimist. Written request received. It will be discussed on Thursday under AOB and I cannot promise anything beyond that.

6ish. i rang the school office and they said parents park there all the time
Parents park there all the time. Yes. They do.
dont be like that

Thursday quorum. Sian confirmed. Me confirmed. Rhys confirmed for 7.45. I will count him as present from when he arrives, and I would be grateful if he did not arrive at 7.46.
